title: Every line on the walls

data.source: 83 Blake lines in use in the museum and the Egg, catalogued by the spiritual lens of the colloquy on 2026-11-18 and compared by its script with public-domain texts (English Wikisource; Sampson 1905, Russell 1906 and a 1906 Boston Marriage from the Internet Archive). Stored catalogue and results in checks/data/cb-every-line/; the fetched texts are not kept in the library.
data.licence: Blake's words are public domain (he died in 1827). The catalogue is the museum's own.

prediction: None about CRR. The lens reported 83 lines: 60 word for word, 2 more once contractions are spelt out, 13 near and 8 not found; the stored file must reproduce that tally, and each near or not-found line's likeness, when worked out again.
baseline: The printed editions themselves. A person with Erdman's standard edition open is the real check; that edition is in copyright and was not fetched.
why: This is not a check of CRR, so no verdict about CRR is possible. It is the museum checking its own walls. 62 of the 83 Blake lines were found word for word, or exactly once contractions are spelt out, in a public-domain text. 13 were near and 8 were not found. No wrong attribution and no invented line was found. Three near lines differ from a 1906 edition by one real word each, and five lines rest on memory alone until someone opens Erdman.
claim_kind: none (not a claim of CRR; the museum checking its own quotations)
operating_characteristics: Not a test of CRR. Nothing here could weigh on it either way.
second_check: The comparison was made by the spiritual lens. This check was written by a different worker from the lens's stored results. No person has yet opened Erdman's edition.

lines.text: The Ruins of Time builds Mansions in Eternity
lines.question: Russell's 1906 Letters print "build". From memory the museum's "builds" is Erdman's reading. Not confirmed: one look at Erdman would settle it.

lines.cite: The Sick Rose, Songs of Experience; stop cites critics
lines.text: O Rose thou art sick. / The invisible worm, / That flies in the night / In the howling storm: / Has found out thy bed / Of crimson joy: / And his dark secret love / Does thy life destroy.
lines.question: Same words; the scan drops the first word and adds a stray mark.

lines.text: For I dance / And drink & sing; / Till some blind hand / Shall brush my wing. / If thought is life / And strength & breath; / And the want / Of thought is death; / Then am I / A happy fly, / If I live, / Or if I die.
lines.question: In Sampson 1905, read there by eye; the scan breaks the stanzas with line numbers and notes.

lines.cite: For the Sexes: The Gates of Paradise (about 1818)
lines.text: Mutual Forgiveness of each Vice / Such are the Gates of Paradise
lines.question: Same words; the scan drops the first word at a page edge.

lines.cite: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, plate 14
lines.text: If the doors of perception were cleansed every thing would appear to man as it is, infinite. / For man has closed himself up, till he sees all things thro narrow chinks of his cavern.
lines.question: Wikisource's copy D of the Marriage spells "til he sees"; the museum has "till". Whether Erdman prints a colon or a comma after "as it is" is also open.

lines.text: The tree which moves some to tears of joy is in the Eyes of others only a Green thing that stands in the way.
lines.question: Russell's 1906 Letters print "which stands in the way". From memory the museum's "that stands" is Erdman's reading. Not confirmed.

lines.text: A Robin Red breast in a Cage / Puts all Heaven in a Rage
lines.question: Same words; the 1905 edition joins "redbreast".

lines.text: Every Night & every Morn / Some to Misery are Born / Every Morn & every Night / Some are Born to sweet delight
lines.question: Same words; the scan reads "Born" as "bom".

lines.text: Hear the voice of the Bard! / Who Present, Past, & Future sees
lines.question: Same words; a stray mark, and the matched passage stops one word short.

lines.text: Piping down the valleys wild / Piping songs of pleasant glee / On a cloud I saw a child. / And he laughing said to me. / Pipe a song about a Lamb; / So I piped with merry chear, / Piper pipe that song again / So I piped, he wept to hear. / Drop thy pipe thy happy pipe / Sing thy songs of happy chear, / So I sung the same again / While he wept with joy to hear / Piper sit thee down and write / In a book that all may read / So he vanish'd from my sight. / And I pluck'd a hollow reed. / And I made a rural pen, / And I stain'd the water clear, / And I wrote my happy songs / Every child may joy to hear
lines.question: In Sampson 1905, read there by eye; the scan breaks the stanzas with line numbers and notes.

lines.text: I have no name / I am but two days old. / What shall I call thee? / I happy am / Joy is my name, / Sweet joy befall thee!
lines.question: Same words; the scan drops the first word.

lines.cite: A Vision of the Last Judgment (1810)
lines.text: When the Sun rises do you not see a round Disk of fire somewhat like a Guinea O no no I see an Innumerable company of the Heavenly host crying Holy Holy Holy is the Lord God Almighty
lines.question: A Vision of the Last Judgment. Not in any text fetched. Rests on memory; needs Erdman or a printing of the Notebook.

lines.text: Ah Sun-flower! weary of time, / Who countest the steps of the Sun
lines.question: Same words; stray marks, and the matched passage stops one word short.

lines.text: Grecian is Mathematic Form / Gothic is Living Form
lines.question: Read by eye in Sampson's note on the Virgil plate; the script could not match it through his editorial marks.

lines.text: Tyger Tyger, burning bright, / In the forests of the night; / What immortal hand or eye, / Could frame thy fearful symmetry?
lines.question: The lens read this as the old edition's modern spelling ("tiger"). The matched passage also has "forest" where the museum has "forests": a person should look at that letter.

lines.text: There is a Void, outside of Existence, which if enterd into / Englobes itself & becomes a Womb
lines.question: Jerusalem, plate 1. Not in the fetched Jerusalem text. Rests on memory.

lines.text: enterd the Door of Death for Albions sake Inspired
lines.question: Jerusalem, plate 1, the erased inscription; many transcriptions leave it out. Rests on memory.

lines.cite: inscription on the engraving Albion rose
lines.text: Albion rose from where he labourd at the Mill with Slaves / Giving himself for the Nations he danc'd the dance of Eternal Death
lines.question: The inscription on the engraving Albion rose. Not in any text fetched. Rests on memory.

lines.text: Heaven opens here on all sides her golden Gates; her windows are not obstructed by vapours; voices of Celestial inhabitants are more distinctly heard, & their forms more distinctly seen.
lines.question: Russell's 1906 Letters print "most distinctly heard". From memory the museum's "more distinctly heard" is Erdman's reading. Not confirmed.

lines.text: In particles bright / The jewels of Light / Distinct shone & clear. / Amaz'd & in fear / I each particle gazed, / Astonish'd, Amazed; / For each was a Man / Human-form'd.
lines.question: Same words; the scan drops the first word and splits "gazed".

lines.cite: A Vision of the Last Judgment, 1810
lines.text: What, it will be Questioned, When the Sun rises, do you not see a round disk of fire somewhat like a Guinea? O no, no, I see an Innumerable company of the Heavenly host
lines.question: The same passage of A Vision of the Last Judgment, spelt "Questioned" in one page and "Questiond" in another. The two pages should agree. Rests on memory.
